title: Contract-based arbitration for continuous batching and KV residency
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: As continuous batching is used to improve GPU utilization, tenant requests compete for limited KV cache residency and GPU memory. Current slot-based preemption leads to oscillation and degraded SLOs for tail-latency sensitive tenants. We need an arbitration mechanism that enforces contracts (SLO commitments + memory/KV allowances) to make preemption decisions predictable, fair, and testable.

Goal: Implement a contract-based arbiter that assigns each tenant a short-lived contract representing a soft budget (tokens for GPU time and KV residency). The arbiter should: (1) honor latency SLOs with probabilistic guarantees, (2) prevent KV thrashing by making eviction decisions contract-aware, (3) allow rapid reclaim for high-priority emergency bursts, and (4) be observable and tunable from Console.

Scope: Design and prototype the arbiter in the continuous-batching runtime, unit tests + integration benchmarks, Console instrumentation (per-tenant contract telemetry), rollout plan for canary on Dedicated pools. Not in scope: long-term multi-cluster global quota management (follow-up project).
acceptance_criteria: A contract allocator component exists in the runtime and emits contracts per tenant with token budgets and kv_target_residency annotation
Preemption decisions reference contract state and are provably bounded (unit tests covering corner cases: eviction under cold-kv, cross-tenant burst, and emergency-preempt)
End-to-end benchmark showing at least 20% reduction in SLO violation rate for 99th-percentile latency on mixed workloads compared to baseline preemptor
Console has a per-tenant contract dashboard (token consumption, kv residency, preemption count) and an alert rule template for high preemption churn
Canary rollout to a single Dedicated pool with automatic rollback on defined regressions
decisions: Use a token-contract model (time tokens + kv-residency credits) rather than strict time-slices to reduce oscillation
Contracts are soft and expire; expiration triggers graceful eviction policies rather than immediate hard termination
Eviction policy will prefer prefix-trimming (when safe) before KV slab eviction to preserve model context where possible
Probabilistic admission: allow occasional contract overcommit (hedging) with exponential backoff to absorb transient bursts
Integration with existing routing layer: contracts are generated by the request admission controller and persisted in the runtime process (no external datastore required for first iteration)
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed — micro-simulator implemented to test token-contract dynamics under synthetic workloads (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/batch-sim, branch: eng/contract-arbiter-spike)
2026-03-01: Design review with Runtime and Console teams — consensus to emit contract telemetry as StatsD + structured logs. Follow-up: add Console wireframe for contract view (design ticket PM-582)

2026-03-05: Prototype PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821) implementing basic token issuance and contract lifecycle hooks. Unit tests added for contract expiry and gentle-evict path.
2026-03-09: Benchmarks (batch-sim) show 12-15% improvement on 99p latency for mixed tail-sensitive workloads. Identified a KV cold-start regression for models with high attention KV footprint.
2026-03-12: Implemented KV admission hinting so contracts can request preferential KV slab region; mitigates cold-start regression in spike tests. Preparing integration tests for Dedicated canary.
2026-03-14: Preparing canary playbook and rollback criteria; Console team started dashboard implementation (Console PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1098).
risks: KV cold-starts if contracts evict aggressively; must tune hold windows to avoid regresses
Incorrect token sizing could starve low-volume but latency-sensitive tenants
Observability gaps could make debugging preemption churn difficult during rollout
Edge-case interaction with autoscaling (Dedicated burst pools) — need to coordinate with autoscaler team
metrics_to_track: rollback_condition: 10% increase in 99p latency for >10 tenants in canary pool
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal Dedicated dev pool canary (1 node) for 48 hours with verbose telemetry; Stage 2: expand to 10% of Dedicated traffic for 72 hours; Stage 3: 100% Dedicated pools behind feature flag. Automated rollback if preemption_count rises >x or 99p latency regression crosses threshold. Post-rollout: run a 7-day soak and compare cost-per-1000-tokens baseline.
